title: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and Concussion
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Severe TBI: reduced consciousness, motor deficits (often both sides), spasticity, abnormal postures, cognitive and behavioural changes, agitation. Concussion: headache, dizziness, nausea, light and noise sensitivity, poor concentration, fatigue, sleep disturbance, emotional change.
qa: What GCS indicates severe TBI? 8 or less.
How do you structure therapy for an agitated patient (Rancho level IV)? Low stimulation, short sessions, simple familiar tasks, consistent staff, safety focus.
Is complete rest best after concussion? No. Short relative rest, then gradual symptom-limited activity.
Why include vestibular and neck examination after concussion? Persistent dizziness and headache often come from these systems.
Older patient on blood thinners becomes drowsy days after a fall? Possible subdural haematoma: emergency.

redFlags.Finding: Drop in GCS, new confusion, unequal pupils
Worsening headache, repeated vomiting, seizure after head injury
Neck pain with limb symptoms after head injury
Clear fluid from nose or ear
Increasing drowsiness in an older patient on anticoagulants days after a fall

manualNotes: Severe TBI: positioning and splinting to prevent contracture; tilt table and early standing when medically cleared; task-specific training; balance and gait; aerobic fitness; high-level mobility (running, jumping) for young patients returning to sport or work.

Vestibular and cervical rehabilitation if dizziness or neck pain persist.
modalityNotes: Splints and serial casting for contracture; FES in selected cases.
